items.text: Document the exports of content, host, node and ship: the content kinds, generators, tuning, flow and diagnostics types and the Vite plugin; the host's analytics properties and test options; the `Files` and `ProcessRunner` services and their live layers; and the ship inputs, `deployDev`, `publishToRuken`, `testRemote`, `rukenToml` and the build checks.

Font subsetting (M5.5): `content/fonts.toml` names each committed source font with its sha256, licence and languages. `automata-content assets` cuts each language's subset to woff2 with a content-hashed name and writes `fonts.json`. A source whose hash differs is refused (`invalidAsset`), and a message with a character none of its language's subsets holds fails at the message's `file:line:col` with the code point (`missingGlyph`). The `./assets` entry adds `buildFonts`, `subsetWoff2` and `fontCoverage`. `CompiledContent.messageLocations` says where each language's message is written.

Atlas packing (M5.6): `content/atlases.toml`, the `@mcthaydt/automata-content/assets` entry (`buildAtlases`, the deterministic `packFrames`), and `automata-content assets`, which writes each atlas page's PNG and Pixi Spritesheet JSON. With a declared `content/palette.toml`, frames are checked against it (`offPalette`); a broken frame is `invalidAsset`.

Content localization (PRODUCT.L2): a translation's missing key is reported at the source text's `file:line:col`, and an extra or non-text key at its own line and column; `CompiledContent` gains `languages` and `catalogs`; `ContentOptions.paraglide` compiles the catalogs (and a game's own) with Paraglide on build; the new `@mcthaydt/automata-content/locale` entry has `createContentText` for run-time lookup and the per-locale glyph sets.
Raise the `vite` peer floor to `^8.3.3`: 8.3.0 to 8.3.2 carry GHSA-587h-7wmj-h5pm (a high-severity `launch-editor` check bypass on Windows, dev server only), which the dependency audit now reports.
Depend on `zod` 4.6.6: 4.6.5 and earlier carry GHSA-mrhx-c7xc-m3w5 (a high-severity memory exhaustion while validating oversized constrained collections), which the dependency audit now reports.

Send the dev server's HMR event only when a rebuild's result actually changed, so one save — which macOS may
report as several watcher events, and which the watcher also emits for authored files at startup — never sends
a second, identical `automata:content` or `automata:content-error`.
@mcthaydt/automata-sim@0.0.2

First published build (M2.4): every package builds to `dist/` with tsdown (ui with svelte-package), bundles the
vendored Ruken code it needs, and publishes to GitHub Packages. `check-boundaries` is now
`@mcthaydt/automata-check-boundaries` with an `automata-check-boundaries` bin.
Make the compiler's skipped-file test portable to a case-insensitive filesystem.

Document the exports of content, host, node and ship: the content kinds, generators, tuning, flow and diagnostics types and the Vite plugin; the host's analytics properties and test options; the `Files` and `ProcessRunner` services and their live layers; and the ship inputs, `deployDev`, `publishToRuken`, `testRemote`, `rukenToml` and the build checks.
`Hosting.saves.keys` lists the session's save keys, sorted; `Hosting.saves.changed` streams another device's write or the host's conflict choice (M5.1).

`Hosting.onExiting` handlers now run one after another in registration order, then the built-in `saves.flush`, all inside one `HOST_EXIT_CAP`, so a write a handler makes is flushed before the host is answered (the SDK ran its exiting listeners together, so the flush could leave first). A handler that never returns costs the flush, and the host is still answered at the cap. Adds `Hosting.round.ended`, a stream with one item per round that ended (its outcome) that ends when Hosting shuts down; a dropped end gives none.

`Hosting.leaderboards.submit/get` relay Ruken's `LeaderboardsApi` (PRODUCT.1). Without the `leaderboards` grant, standalone or offline they fail with the SDK's code as a `HostError`; nothing falls back to a local board.

PUB.1: a web `Hosting` adapter for builds published outside Ruken (itch.io or any static host), chosen at build time through the new `@mcthaydt/automata-host/target` export (`automata-web` condition → web adapter, `default` → Ruken adapter). `Hosting.kind` gains `'web'` and `Hosting.hostName` names the host for UI. `RUKEN_SDK_MARKERS` and `findRukenSdkMarkers` let a build check that an itch bundle holds no Ruken SDK code.

Document the exports of content, host, node and ship: the content kinds, generators, tuning, flow and diagnostics types and the Vite plugin; the host's analytics properties and test options; the `Files` and `ProcessRunner` services and their live layers; and the ship inputs, `deployDev`, `publishToRuken`, `testRemote`, `rukenToml` and the build checks.
EX.2: the reference games moved to `games/` (`games/emberwick`, `games/placeholder`); ship's port and `test-remote` notes name the new paths. No API change.

`inputsProblems(inputs, bindings)` checks `runtime.inputs` against a game's input bindings (M4 spec §4.13): pad buttons need `"gamepad"`, and `"touch"` needs a touch button or a gesture. `prepareBuild` takes an optional `inputBindings` and fails with the new `ManifestInputsMismatch` before writing `ruken.toml`. Additive: without `inputBindings`, prepare behaves as before.

`runtime.inputs` against the game's input map without loading it (M4.1 follow-up): `prepare` (when the caller gives no `inputBindings`) and the private `automata check` (a new `inputs` step, rule `inputs-mismatch`) read the `keys()` calls in the game's sources, as the board and orientation checks read theirs, and apply `inputsProblems` to what they bind: a pad binding with no `gamepad`, or `touch` with nothing to touch. Anything not written as a literal counts as touchable and binds no pad, so a reported problem is always real. `ship` exports `keysBindingsIn`, `declaredInputsIn`, `findInputsProblems`, `isInputsSource` and `DeclaredInputs`.

The game's orientation against the ship config (M4.7 follow-up): `prepare` fails with `OrientationMismatch`, and the private `automata check` gains an `orientation` step (rule `orientation-mismatch`), when a `defineGame` plays in an `orientation` other than `ship.config.ts`'s `runtime.orientation` (`any` when the game leaves it out). The sources are read, not run, as the board check reads them, so only string literals are compared. `ship` exports `gameOrientationsIn`, `declaredOrientationIn`, `findOrientationMismatches`, `isOrientationSource` and their types.

M5.7 leaderboard flow. ui: `LeaderboardPanel` (loading, entries with the player's row marked, empty, unavailable, offline) and its `LeaderboardView`, `LeaderboardEntryView` and `LeaderboardCopy` types. ship: `prepareBuild` refuses a game that names a leaderboard its ship config does not declare (`UndeclaredBoard`, with the call site), and exports the scan (`findUndeclaredBoards`, `boardNamesIn`, `declaredBoardsIn`, `isBoardSource`). (The cli's new `automata check` step `boards`, rule `undeclared-board`, needs no changeset: the cli is private.) Additive for every caller.

Add `--target itch` to `automata-ship prepare` and `publish`: itch.io's index.html, limit, case and ruken.toml checks, a byte-reproducible `<id>-<version>-itch.zip`, and `butler push` with `--userversion` and `--if-changed`. `ShipConfig` gains an optional `itch` section. The Ruken path is unchanged.

`prepare` (and so `publish` and `deploy-dev`) now fails when the build holds a secret: a known key format (Stripe, AWS, GitHub, npm, private keys and others, named by their gitleaks rule IDs), the value of any variable in the game folder's `.env*` files, or a high-entropy quoted string. The error names the file, line, column and byte offset, never the secret. The scanner is exported as `scanTextForSecrets`, `findSecretsInBuild`, `readEnvValues` and `parseEnvFile` (QB.2).

The release workflow's version commit carries `[skip ci]`, so a push to the Version packages branch starts no
`ci`, `parity`, game-ci or consumer-smoke run (the release job checks and publishes the commit itself).
Depend on `zod` 4.6.6: 4.6.5 and earlier carry GHSA-mrhx-c7xc-m3w5 (a high-severity memory exhaustion while validating oversized constrained collections), which the dependency audit now reports.

Inside AF, an example's game-ci job skips `Check` and the determinism checker (the `checks` job already runs
them for every package), and `ci:local` stops repeating base-2d's check.
Make the deploy test's tarball fixtures portable to bsdtar (macOS `tar`).

`goldenCommands({ root })` lets the browser golden read command serve golden files from a folder wider than the Vitest project's root, for a package whose goldens sit beside it (the examples runner reads `examples/__goldens__`). Additive: `goldenCommands()` keeps the project root.

Document the exports of testing and physics: the viewport, resize-observer and mount fixtures, the reference sizes and variants, the golden and snapshot round-trip checks and their reports; and the physics kinds, spawn helpers, options and collision events, in 2D and 3D.

The input × form-factor matrix (M4.10): a new `@mcthaydt/automata-testing/e2e` entry with `FakePad` (a standard controller for a real built game, from FloorFifty's fake gamepad, reachable in the game's frame under a host), the touch helpers `tap`, `hold`, `swipe` and `flick`, and `INPUT_MATRIX`, the M4 spec's cells as data; and `@mcthaydt/automata-testing/input` with `fakeGamepads()`, a `navigator.getGamepads` stand-in for unit tests. `@playwright/test` is an optional peer, needed only by the `e2e` entry. The private runtime and game packages gain the active device following the host's input mode (`makeInput({ hostInput })`) and the "This controller isn't supported yet" toast for a pad without the standard mapping.

Document the exports of ui: the geometry owner and its types, the device, form factor and height tier classifiers, the landscape gate, the focus navigator, the input method tracker, the hidden browser bar, the action bar and boot failure types, and the `@component` comments of ActionBar, CornerControls, Dialog, ErrorPanel, BootFailurePanel, LoaderOverlay, ScreenFrame and ScrollList.
Add BootDefect support to boot failure panel so unexpected runtime defects render with full error details and retry support.

Touch input (M4.3): `TouchControls`, sticky on-screen buttons that hold an action while any finger is on them and hide without remounting; `SwipeSurface`, which forwards fingers to a gesture tracker and draws the thumb's line; and the `PointerLatch`, `StickyPointers` and `nearestTarget` bookkeeping behind them.

Rebinding and Settings (M4.4): `Prompt` and its labels (`keyLabel`, `padLabel`, `promptView`, `readKeyboardLayout`); `ControlsSection`, `DisplaySection` and the core `SettingsScreen`, whose sections are the screen's snippets or an extension's `settings.sections` components. The private runtime and game packages gain the saved bindings (`inputSettingsSchema`, `applyOverrides`, `rebindProfile`, `Input.rebind`, `resetBindings`, `capture`), the core settings (`CORE_SETTINGS`), `keys()` labels, and the default Settings screen reached from paused.

M4.5 focus, back and cursor: `FocusNavigator` gains `steer` (spatial inside a `[data-focus-grid]`, DOM order elsewhere), `page`, `adjust` and the keyboard repeat `guard`. New exports: `sendBack` and `interceptBackGesture` (the system back gesture as Back, history key `afBackGuard`), `CursorRunner`, `cursorHidden` and `CURSOR_IDLE_MS` (an idle pointer hides on `gameplay` screens only), and the paging helpers `isTap`, `releaseStep`, `WheelPager` and `PAGE_SWIPE`. Additive for every caller.

Adds the M4.6 primitives: `Split`, `OptionGroup`, `PagerDots`, `PagedGrid` (with `paginate`, `fitShape`, `tileSide`, `trimRows`, `fitColumns`, `pageOf` and `wrapPage`), `Button`, `IconButton`, `Toggle`, `Slider`, `Chip`, `Modal`, `Sheet` and `Toast`, with the `--af-success` and `--af-danger-edge` theme tokens. `Dialog` now shares its modal scoping with `Modal` and `Sheet`; its behaviour is unchanged. Every visible string is a prop, and a nameless `IconButton` or a toned `Chip` or `Toast` without its `toneLabel` throws while it mounts.

Display policy (M4.7): `LandscapeGate` and `RotateHint`, standalone fullscreen (`fullscreenSupport`, `isFullscreen`, `onFullscreenChange`, `enterFullscreen`), and the touch overlay's reduced set: a `TouchButtonSpec` marked `required` stays when the buttons do not all fit, never shrunk. The touch group's sticky margin no longer reaches over what sits above it, and the layout contract reports a control under a touch button. The private runtime and game packages gain the display policy (the landscape gate standalone only, the rotate hint pausing under `display`), `GameSpec.orientation`, `keys()`'s `required`, and the play screen's `hud.overlay` slot.

Adds `SaveStatus` and `SaveSlots` for a game's saves (M5.2). `SaveStatus` says the host's save state in words (checking, syncing, saved, offline, retrying, conflict, recovered, or "no grant") in a polite live region that is not focusable, and renders nothing where there is no status (standalone). `SaveSlots` is the slot list: rows are chosen, and the chosen row's actions (Continue, New game, Delete… behind a confirming dialog whose safe button has focus) sit in an action bar; the rows scroll in their own list and a label and a time wrap to two lines. Both take the caller's words and times, and read no store. Also exports the types `SaveStatusState`, `SaveStatusCopy`, `SaveSlotView`, `SaveSlotsView`, `SaveSlotsCopy` and `SaveSlotActivity`, and the helpers `SAVE_STATUS_TONES`, `defaultSlot` and `slotActionsOf`.

The Audio settings group (M5.4): `AudioSection`, laid out as FloorFifty's (Mute, Mute in the background, a slider per bus with its percentage; unavailable when sound could not start; a note while the host's volume is down), with `AudioCopy`, `AudioValue`, `AudioSectionChange`, `AudioBus` and `AUDIO_BUSES`. `Slider` gains `layout: 'row'` (name, track and value on one row).

M5.7 leaderboard flow. ui: `LeaderboardPanel` (loading, entries with the player's row marked, empty, unavailable, offline) and its `LeaderboardView`, `LeaderboardEntryView` and `LeaderboardCopy` types. ship: `prepareBuild` refuses a game that names a leaderboard its ship config does not declare (`UndeclaredBoard`, with the call site), and exports the scan (`findUndeclaredBoards`, `boardNamesIn`, `declaredBoardsIn`, `isBoardSource`). (The cli's new `automata check` step `boards`, rule `undeclared-board`, needs no changeset: the cli is private.) Additive for every caller.

The boot-failure panel's exit button names the host and needs the `exit` grant: `BootFailurePanel` takes `hostName` and `canExit`, `bootFailureView` takes `canExit`, the default copy is `Back to {host}` (filled by the new `withHostName`), and "Back to …" is never drawn when the host did not grant `exit`. The (unpublished) runtime passes them from `Hosting`. Inside Ruken, which always grants `exit`, the panel still says "Back to Ruken".

Settings and Pause, laid out as FloorFifty's (Owner, 2026-10-18): `SettingsScreen` is a dialog of tabs (`SettingsTab`: Settings, Controls) over the dimmed game; `ControlsSection` has one section per device, the one in use first and marked, with one rebind button a row; `TouchSection` is the Touch controls group. `Modal` gains `head` (beside the title on a wide dialog) and `wide` (widens on a short band), and keeps room for a focused control's ring. `ControlsCopy` gains `touch` and `inUse` and loses `touchMode` and `touchModes` (now `TouchCopy`). The private game package's Paused screen becomes FloorFifty's pause dialog, with Quit asking first.
